question_text: Calculate the number of atoms in 100 g of silver (Ag). The atomic mass of silver is $107.868 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ and the Avogadro constant is $6.022 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{atoms} / \mathrm{mol}$.
response:
The number of atoms is found from:

$$N = \frac{m}{M}\,N_A = \frac{100\ \mathrm{g}}{107.868\ \mathrm{g/mol}}\times 6.022\times10^{23}\ \mathrm{atoms/mol} \approx 5.58\times10^{23}\ \mathrm{atoms}$$

$$\boxed{5.58 \times 10^{23}}$$
